name: Hotel Bel-Air
address: 701 Stone Canyon Road, Los Angeles, CA 90077, United States
tagline: 103 rooms and suites in twelve acres of garden, with a swan lake and an oval pool.
description:
Hotel Bel-Air is a Dorchester Collection hotel at 701 Stone Canyon Road in the Bel-Air hills of Los Angeles, a mile west of Beverly Hills. It has 103 rooms and suites in twelve acres of gardens, with a lake of swans, and most rooms opening directly onto the grounds.

The main building began as the estate office of Alphonzo Bell, who bought 600 acres west of Los Angeles and named the area Bel-Air. The Texan hotelier Joseph Drown bought 18 acres including that building in 1946 and, working with the architect Burton Schutt, opened the hotel on 24 August of that year. Dorchester Collection took it on in 2008 and, with the designer Alexandra Champalimaud and the Rockwell Group, renovated all 103 rooms and the public spaces over two years.

The Superior Room has 40 square metres and a garden view. The Canyon Studio, at 60 square metres, has retractable walls onto a private patio with a plunge pool and outdoor fireplace. The Swan Lake Suite, 70 square metres, sits above the lake. The Grace Kelly Suite has 85 square metres, vaulted ceilings, a private patio with a plunge pool and a jacuzzi. The Bell Suite, 167 square metres, has an engraved wooden ceiling, a private elevator and a dining room for eight, and the Presidential Suite covers 210 square metres around a private courtyard with an infinity pool and a grand piano. Complimentary round-trip airport transfers come with the larger suites.

The Restaurant at Hotel Bel-Air serves breakfast, lunch, dinner and weekend brunch, and still serves the tortilla soup that first appeared on its menu in 1980. The Bar and Lounge, for adults, has live music each evening and Norman Seeff's photographs of musicians on the walls. Afternoon tea is served in The Living Room from Friday to Sunday, and there is a patisserie on site.

The oval pool, 23 by 10 metres and heated to 27.8 degrees Celsius, was a horse-riding ring before Joseph Drown rebuilt the grounds. It is open to hotel guests daily from 8 am to 6 pm. The Spa at Hotel Bel-Air uses Valmont products and has seven treatment rooms and a private enclave with a marble soaking tub, and the gym is open around the clock. A house car takes guests anywhere within three miles. Los Angeles International Airport is about 30 to 40 minutes away.

The hotel suits travellers who want a private, green setting in the hills, ten minutes by car from Rodeo Drive.
